macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as tech sell-off deepens
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.1% and the S&P 500 dropped 1.1% on Friday as declines in major technology and chip stocks weighed on markets. The S&P 500 posted an approximately 2% weekly loss, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.5% for the session.[3][4]

items.title: Fed chair offers no guidance on upcoming rate decision
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh declined to prejudge upcoming interest-rate decisions while expressing optimism about U.S. economic strength. Markets increasingly expect rates to remain unchanged at the October meeting, while expectations for a December hike have risen amid stronger inflation data.[3][5]

items.title: U.S. inflation pressures intensify
items.summary: September producer prices rose 6.3% year over year, the largest increase since December 2022, while import prices increased 1.1% in the month and 8.1% from a year earlier. The data strengthened expectations that the Fed could raise rates later this year.[8][9]

items.title: Tesla shares pressured after futuristic Roadster unveiling
items.summary: Tesla shares declined after the company unveiled a redesigned Roadster featuring rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX. The vehicle is not expected to enter production until 2028.[3][5]

items.title: Alcoa and Travelers beat quarterly earnings expectations
items.summary: Alcoa rose 2.5% and Travelers gained 1.5% after reporting quarterly results above Wall Street forecasts. Travelers reported adjusted earnings per share of $9.18 versus a $7.25 consensus estimate, with revenue of $12.41 billion.[3][9]

items.title: Indonesia faces possible emerging-market downgrade
items.summary: Indonesia’s stock market plunged after MSCI warned that it could downgrade the country from emerging-market status, adding to broader pressure in global equities.[8]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds to about $82,000 as major cryptocurrencies recover
items.summary: Bitcoin rose roughly 1.9% to $82,130, while Ether gained 3.6% to $2,443. XRP, Solana, Cardano and BNB also advanced, although several remained lower for the week.

items.title: Crypto market faces Federal Reserve and regulatory uncertainty
items.summary: Bitcoin remained in an approximately $80,000-$88,000 range as traders assessed ETF outflows and the Federal Reserve’s upcoming decision. U.S. crypto legislation remains stalled following the departure of White House negotiator Patrick Witt.

items.title: Australia consults on capital requirements for crypto platforms
items.summary: Australia’s securities regulator is consulting on new capital models for crypto platforms, including a proposed requirement of at least A$14 million or 10% of average revenue when qualifying outsourced custody is unavailable.

items.title: U.S. crypto market-structure legislation remains divided
items.summary: The Senate Agriculture Committee advanced the Commodity Futures Trading Commission-focused portion of a market-structure bill, while the Senate Banking Committee had not yet voted on the broader CLARITY Act. Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong criticized the draft over potential effects on tokenized equities, DeFi and stablecoin rewards.

items.title: SEC clarifies securities-law treatment of tokenized assets
items.summary: SEC staff issued guidance addressing how existing securities laws apply to tokenized securities, as U.S. policymakers continue debating oversight of digital-asset markets.

items.title: Blur plans to shut down its front end and halt new Blend loan matching
items.summary: NFT marketplace Blur reportedly plans to close its front end in November 2026, while its Blend NFT-lending protocol will stop matching new loans.

items.title: Zcash leads major-token gains
items.summary: Zcash rose about 12% to approximately $1,222 in Asian trading, outperforming other major cryptocurrencies as Bitcoin and leading altcoins recovered.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open AI model
items.summary: Meta reportedly unveiled Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight mixture-of-experts model aimed at coding and agentic workloads. The model was described as the most capable U.S. open-weight model to date, though independent benchmarks were not provided in the available coverage.

items.title: Elorian launches Glimpse visual-thinking model
items.summary: Elorian reportedly released Glimpse, a multimodal model designed to repeatedly re-inspect images and video while reasoning. The approach targets more deliberate visual analysis rather than one-pass interpretation.

items.title: Google DeepMind agent reports mathematical breakthroughs
items.summary: Google DeepMind’s AlphaProof Nexus reportedly solved nine of 353 open Erdős problems and proved 44 of 492 OEIS conjectures autonomously, according to coverage of a new arXiv paper. The reported cost was a few hundred dollars per problem.

items.title: Constructor introduces agentic checkout
items.summary: Constructor announced Agentic Checkout, an integration with Stripe that lets shoppers and AI agents discover and purchase products within a single conversational interface.

items.title: AI safety and financial concerns intensify
items.summary: Coverage highlighted growing scrutiny of AI-agent incidents, lawsuits alleging harms to children from ChatGPT, and investor concerns about slowing revenue growth at leading AI companies. AI labs are nevertheless continuing to release models and emphasize open-weight systems for enterprise customization.

items.title: BrainChip introduces Sequora edge-AI processor IP
items.summary: BrainChip launched Sequora, a processor intellectual-property core designed for generative AI applications on battery-powered edge devices. The announcement reflects continuing industry investment in lower-power, on-device AI hardware.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: US lawmaker proposes bill to give game buyers ownership
items.summary: Rep. Ritchie Torres introduced the proposed Power to Players Act, which would direct the FTC to create protections preventing publishers from removing access to purchased games when online services shut down. The proposal follows concerns over games becoming unplayable after server closures.[1][2]

items.title: CD Projekt Red shares development update on Project Hadar
items.summary: CD Projekt Red said its original intellectual property, codenamed Project Hadar, is being prototyped and benchmarked with Unreal Engine. The game has not yet entered full pre-production.[10]

items.title: Epic plans Fortnite release on AltStore while leaving Samsung Galaxy Store
items.summary: Epic Games plans to bring Fortnite to AltStore and is withdrawing its games from Samsung’s Galaxy Store, citing objections to mobile storefront business practices.[3]

items.title: Xbox Nano Controller announced for November launch
items.summary: Microsoft introduced the Xbox Nano Controller, a compact controller designed for portable and multi-device gaming. It is scheduled to launch November 4, 2026, at $49.99.[4]

items.title: Nintendo shows more of Ocarina of Time Remake
items.summary: Nintendo released additional details and footage of its upcoming Ocarina of Time Remake, including expanded looks at Hyrule, Link’s combat with Dark Link, and new fairy hints. The game is scheduled for November 5, 2026, with a physical edition planned.[4]

items.title: Peak coming to consoles with cross-play
items.summary: The co-op survival game Peak is scheduled to release on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and Switch 2 on October 22, with cross-play support.[9]

items.title: Ubisoft reportedly preparing more than 200 layoffs
items.summary: A report says Ubisoft is preparing to cut more than 200 jobs as the publisher continues restructuring efforts.[5]
